sections.overview: The Mangshan pit viper is a venomous snake restricted to a small area of the Nanling Mountains in southern China.
sections.identification: It is a member of Viperidae, subfamily Crotalinae, the pit vipers.
sections.habitat: Accounts place it in moist subtropical forest around Mount Mang and nearby parts of the Nanling range, in Hunan and Guangdong.
sections.diet: The sources used here do not provide enough species-specific evidence for a reliable summary of its wild diet.
sections.behavior: A telemetry study documents seasonal activity and habitat use, but this brief account does not generalize its findings beyond the monitored snakes and study area.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted do not establish a sufficiently detailed account of reproduction for this profile.
sections.ecology: Its narrow range and habitat pressures make protection of the remaining forest important; collection for the wildlife trade has also been identified as a threat.
sections.conservation: The IUCN lists it as Endangered. China also includes it among its highest-level nationally protected wildlife.
